title: What to Evaluate in Low-Cost Process Management Tools
summary: See what to evaluate in low-cost process management tools before switching, without comparing mismatched plans.
body_markdown:
Evaluating **low-cost process management tools** means looking beyond the advertised monthly fee: per-user versus per-process pricing, the cost of intermediaries like Zapier or Make, and how much manual work the tool still leaves behind. **Jestor** charges per user, with native automations included.


The real cost of a tool rarely shows up in full in the first proposal. It shows up later, as a paid plugin, an extra integration, or manual hours the automation didn't cover.


That's why, before switching just for a lower price, it's worth understanding what's actually included.


## What Usually Inflates the Real Cost


- Charging per automation, process, or "workflow," instead of per user
- Needing Zapier, Make, or another paid intermediary to integrate with the ERP
- Plans that cap the number of automations or integrations at the cheapest tier
- Lack of native integration, creating manual work hours that never show up on the invoice


## How to Evaluate the Real Cost


1. Add the tool's monthly fee to the cost of any intermediary needed to integrate with the ERP
2. Check whether the cheapest plan limits automations, users, or important integrations
3. Calculate how many hours of manual work would still exist even with the tool in place
4. Confirm whether pricing changes when adding more ERP accounts, branches, or company IDs
5. Always compare equivalent plans, never a free plan from one tool against the full plan of another


Type of cost Where it usually shows up


Per-automation billing The invoice grows with usage, not with the team


Integration intermediary Extra subscription for Zapier, Make, or similar


Remaining manual work Doesn't show on the invoice, but consumes team hours


Cost per connected ERP account Grows as the company opens branches or company IDs


## Why Jestor Tends to Be More Predictable


- Billing is per **user** , not per number of connected ERP accounts, working with one or several at no added cost
- More than 400 native **automations** included, without relying on Zapier, Make, or another paid intermediary
- Native integration with Omie and Conta Azul, with no external connector cost
- The **Jestor** team helps with initial setup at no charge

## Frequently asked questions


**Is the cheapest tool always the most economical in the end?** Not always, because intermediary costs and remaining manual work often stay out of the advertised price.


**Does Jestor charge per automation used?** No, billing is per user; see details at[jestor.com](https://www.jestor.com/?ref=blog.jestor.com) .


**Do additional ERP accounts increase the cost of Jestor?** No, the platform works with one or several ERP accounts at no extra cost per account.


**Is it worth comparing a free plan from one tool with a paid plan from another?** No, that comparison is unbalanced; the right approach is always comparing equivalent plans.


Evaluating **low-cost process management tools** by total cost, not just the monthly fee, is what keeps you from an expensive switch later.
